<description>
Introduced in #36475:
```bash
/ci_container_base/src/bench/bip352.cpp:22:12: error: type ‘InputType’ violates the C++ One Definition Rule [-Werror=odr]
   22 | enum class InputType {
      |            ^
/ci_container_base/src/bench/sign_transaction.cpp:24:12: note: an enum with different value name is defined in another translation unit
   24 | enum class InputType {
      |            ^
/ci_container_base/src/bench/bip352.cpp:23:5: note: name ‘P2PKH’ differs from name ‘P2WPKH’ defined in another translation unit
   23 |     P2PKH,           // legacy pubkey-hash
      |     ^
/ci_container_base/src/bench/sign_transaction.cpp:25:5: note: mismatching definition
   25 |     P2WPKH, // segwitv0, witness-pubkey-hash (ECDSA signature)
      |     ^
```

There's a commit here that adds a CI config, using GCC and LTO, which uses `-Wodr`. The existing LTO config uses Clang, and I'm not sure about adding LTO to any existing job. However I do think we should be catching ODR violations in CI.
</description>

<commits>
307b22b59d bench: put InputType enums in anonymous namespaces

Fixes an ODR violation.

66654bc5ce ci: add CMAKE_INTERPROCEDURAL_OPTIMIZATION to Alpine job
</commits>
